title: A loop with one half-twist has only one side
body: Give a strip of paper a half-twist before joining its ends, and you make a **Möbius strip**. A line drawn along its middle can travel across what looked like both sides of the paper and return to its start without crossing an edge. The half-twist connects those apparent sides into one continuous surface. The strip also has just one continuous boundary edge.

slides.heading: Make the shape
items: Take a long rectangular strip of paper.
Turn one end through half a turn: 180 degrees.
Join the short ends to make a loop.

slides.heading: Try the pencil test
slides.text: Start a line in the middle and keep going around the loop. You can return to the start after visiting both original faces, without lifting the pencil or crossing an edge.

left.label: Untwisted loop
left.text: Two sides and two separate boundary edges.

right.label: Möbius strip
right.text: One continuous side and one continuous boundary edge.

slides.question: How many boundary edges does a Möbius strip have?
slides.explanation: The half-twist joins what looked like two edges into one continuous boundary, just as it joins the two apparent sides into one surface. An untwisted loop has two edges.

slides.heading: Plain loop or Möbius strip?

items.text: A centre line comes back without crossing an edge
Made with a half-twist before joining

slides.explanation: The half-twist joins the two apparent sides into one surface, and the two edges into one boundary.
